summary: @servicetitan/hammer-token preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"` in package.json. setup.mjs is an obfuscated launcher (hex-mangled identifiers, string-lookup dispatcher) that downloads the Bun runtime from the oven-sh/bun v1.3.13 GitHub release and then invokes the downloaded bun binary via `execFileSync` against the sibling file `math_init.js`, a 727 KB bun-compiled JavaScript bundle shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is heavily obfuscated using string-array rotation (`WV8StW` rotator, hex-mangled identifiers, a mixed literal table) with no readable code paths; all strings including any network destinations are reconstructed at runtime. The advertised purpose of the package is Figma design tokens, which has no legitimate need for an alternate language runtime or a compiled opaque payload executed at install time. The choice of a bun-compiled bundle specifically evades inspection by Node-based scanners. The package also contains a token-handling utility at src/utils/figma/get-token.js that reads local files and issues HTTP POSTs, but the primary installer-side execution surface is the preinstall path, which runs attacker-controlled opaque code on every `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
